one_paragraph: After this work, two fingers moved upward on the page bring up a Links bar along the bottom. It lists the Index entries that this page links to, numbered in reading order. Tap an entry and the page above the bar turns into that page straight away, with no flash. Tap the page to stay there, or close the bar to go back to where you started. Hold an entry, or hold a finger on a link on the page, and a dotted border shows exactly what counts as tappable. A small card opens next to it with Rename, Change where it goes, Redraw the area and Delete link, and the page stays in view the whole time. Making a link no longer leaves ink. You circle the words, a dashed line follows the pen but is never ink, and you pick where it goes from Recent targets or the Index, or make a new page and name it. Your existing beta.5 links keep working: each one's circle becomes its tappable area the first time its page opens, and the circle stays on the page as ordinary ink. Two fingers moved down open the Pages view, and two fingers to the left or right turn the page. Settings gets a Gestures button between Controller and Updates: tap an action, do the gesture, and if Grimoire refuses it, it says why. Every toggle and important setting becomes an action you can bind to a gesture, a key, a controller button, and later the pen's button. Smart shapes snap a box, circle, triangle or line only when you hold the pen still and the shape really is one. Moving on brings your own line back, and one Undo removes the shape. The Index button opens a map of the whole notebook as dots. Well-linked pages are solid, lightly linked ones are dithered, and unlinked pages are small hollow rings beside their section. It ships in seven Kindle builds, and you test each one. The first fixes the touch input and records how your panel behaves. The second brings gestures and the Links bar, then come ink-free links with the long-press card, then Settings > Gestures, then Smart shapes, then the map, and last the pen-button gestures.

plan.experience:
Upright unless said otherwise. Sizes are px at 300 dpi (11.8 px per mm); text is 44 px, titles 64 px, small text 34 px. [Pn] names the build that brings each part.

0. AFTER THE UPDATE [P2]
- The first time a notebook opens, one two-line toast shows for 6 s: 'New: two fingers up show this page's links. Two fingers down show all pages.' / 'Novedad: dos dedos hacia arriba muestran los enlaces de esta página; hacia abajo, todas las páginas.' This is settings.ini hints bit 0.
- The panel has a new Links button under Next: a chain glyph (question 7). A 7 px solid dot in its corner means this page has links. P5 adds a Shapes button under the eraser.

1. OPENING THE LINKS BAR [P2]
- Open it with two fingers up anywhere on the upright, fitted page, with the Links button, or with the 'links' action from a key, a controller button, or later a pen button.
- When the fingers lift, a card rises from the bottom in one GL16 refresh: about 0.35 s, no flash.
- Header: 'Links on this page (3)' / 'Enlaces de esta página (3)', with an X at the right.
- Below the header: numbered chips in reading order, one per Index entry this page links to (question 1). For example: '1 Meeting notes   p. 12', '2 Page 20   p. 20', '3 The Index'.
  - Two links to the same entry show once, marked '×2'.
  - The eye draws the same numbers on the page.
- Bottom row, four labelled buttons: Go to (a magnifier), New link (a chain with a plus), Areas (an eye, dimmed while off) and Index (three bubbles).
- On an empty page: 'No links on this page yet.' / 'Esta página aún no tiene enlaces.', with New link shown as the main, inverted button.
- The first 3 times, the header adds a hint: 'Tap a link to look. Tap the page to stay.'

2. HOPPING (PEEK) [P2]
- Tap chip 1. It inverts at once (DU) and the page above the bar becomes page 12, with a GL16 of that area only.
  - About 0.4 s, because it was rendered in the background while you looked.
  - The first time, a dense or PDF page can take up to 1.2 s; the inverted chip shows the wait.
  - The panel's page chip shows 12.
- The header becomes '‹ Page 3   Showing Meeting notes. Tap the page to stay.' with the X.
- The chips are still page 3's links, so tapping chip 2 shows page 20 instead.
- To stay: tap the page above the bar with a finger. It counts when the finger lifts.
  - The bar closes and page 20 becomes the open page.
  - One GC16 flash marks the arrival and clears any ghosting from the peeks.
  - That tap does nothing else: it never follows a link or presses a panel button.
  - A pen touch there also stays, and its stroke is not drawn.
  - A tap on the panel also stays, and the button is not pressed.
- To go back:
  - '‹ Page 3' shows page 3 again and keeps the bar open.
  - X, two fingers down, the Links button again, Close menu or the Back key close the bar and return to page 3 exactly as you left it, zoom included.
  - That return is GL16, or GC16 after 3 or more peeks, to clear ghosting.
- Anything that acts on the page you see stays on it first: New link, Go to, Index, or another menu's button or key.
- Peeks never write notebook.ini. If the Kindle sleeps, powers off or crashes during a peek, the notebook reopens on page 3.

3. HOLDING A LINK (THE SECOND RULING) [P3]
- Hold a finger still on a link for 0.6 s.
  - A heavy dotted border appears around the link's area at once, in about 0.2 s. Only the four border strips are refreshed, by DU.
  - Then a small card opens beside the area by GL16: to the right if it fits, else left, below, above.
  - The notebook page stays in view.
- The card (780 x 666):
  - Title: 'Meeting notes · p. 12'.
  - Rename in the Index. For an unnamed page it reads 'Add page 20 to the Index...'. A link to The Index has no rename row.
  - Change where it goes...
  - Redraw the area
  - Delete link
- Rename: the keyboard opens over the page, with the card and the border still visible above it. Done shows 'Page 12 is in the Index as Meeting notes.'
- Change where it goes: Link to... opens with the current target marked.
- Redraw the area: you draw a new area for this same link.
- Delete link: 'Link deleted. Undo brings it back.' / 'Enlace borrado. Deshacer lo recupera.' A border you drew yourself is ink, and it stays.
- A tap outside closes the card and does nothing else.
- On a read-only page the card shows only the target, with the line 'This page is read-only.'
- In the bar, holding a chip for 0.6 s opens the same card, above the bar.
  - If you are peeking, the bar first returns to the page the links are on.
  - The entry's areas get the dotted border.
  - A '×2' entry offers 'Delete 2 links' and 'Change where they go', and adds the line 'To change one, hold it on the page.'

4. MAKING A LINK, WITHOUT INK [P3; in P2, New link still uses today's flow]
1. Tap New link in the bar, use the 'add-link' action, or tap 'Add a link' on the Index tab.
2. The bar folds into a 130 px strip at the bottom: 'Draw around what links.' / 'Rodea lo que enlaza.', with Cancel.
3. Circle the words with the pen. A dashed 4 px line follows the nib by DU. It is screen UI, never ink.
4. When you lift, the dashes become a dotted rectangle around the circle's box.
5. Link to... opens at the bottom, or at the top when your rectangle is in the lower part of the screen, so it stays visible.
   - Chips: New page..., The Index, up to 4 Recent targets, then the Index entries, paged.
   - Tool row: Search, Choose from the pages..., Cancel.
6. Tap 'Meeting notes'.
   - The toast says 'Linked to Meeting notes.'
   - The dotted rectangle goes away unless Areas is on.
   - The page looks exactly as it did before.
   - If you started from the bar, the bar comes back with the new entry.
   - One Undo removes the link.
Other outcomes:
- New page...: a keyboard over the page asks 'Name the new page'.
  - Done appends a page at the end of the notebook, so page numbers never move. It names the page, making it a new Index entry, and links to it. You stay where you are: 'Linked to the new page 53.'
  - Cancel makes no page.
- Too small (under 5 mm both ways): 'Too small for a link: draw around what links.' Link mode stays on.
- Cancel: 'No link made.'
- A refusal always says why: the page is read-only, links.ini cannot be read, or the page already has 64 links.

5. FOLLOWING
- A finger tap inside a link's area goes there with a GC16 flash, as today.
- Where areas are nested, the smallest one under the finger wins.
- The pen always writes, even on a link.

6. SEEING AREAS [P2]
- Areas, in the bar, draws a dashed outline and a numbered tag on every link area of the page. The numbers match the chips.
- The choice is remembered.
- The outlines are never drawn into the page, the PDF, the thumbnails or the sleep image.
- The first time, a tip: 'Dotted boxes show where a finger tap follows a link. They never print.'

7. VISIBLE BORDERS
A visible border is ink you draw yourself; Smart shapes make a clean box. It is never part of the link: erasing it keeps the link, and deleting the link keeps the border.

8. GO TO [P2]
- Open it from the bar's Go to, from 'Go to page...' in the Pages view, or with the 'go-to-page' action.
- A keyboard opens over the page, with the field 'Page number or name'.
  - Typing '12' puts 'Go to page 12' first.
  - Typing 'reu' lists 'Reunión': accents and case are ignored.
- Tapping a result goes there (GC16), and the page you left goes on the back list.

9. PAGES VIEW AND PAGE TURNS [P2]
- Two fingers down open the Pages view (GC16); two fingers up close it.
- Two fingers left or right turn the page (question 5). At the end of the notebook: 'This is the last page.' A gesture never adds a page; the panel's + still does.

10. SIDEWAYS OR ZOOMED IN [P2]
- Where the page can scroll, a two-finger drag in mid-screen pans as today, now without the zoom drifting.
- Navigation swipes start in an edge band: 25 mm at the top and bottom, 15 mm at the sides (question 4).
- The first time a drag scrolls instead of opening something, a tip: 'To open Pages or links here, start at the top or bottom edge.'

11. SMART SHAPES [P5]
- Draw a box and hold the nib still for 0.55 s. One DU frame shows a clean rectangle in the same pen and size.
- Lift to keep it. Move on instead and your own line comes back, and the stroke simply continues.
- Handwriting never snaps.
- One Undo removes the shape.
- The panel's Shapes button toggles the feature: a filled glyph when on, an outline with a slash when off, never inverted.
- The tool picker gets a row reading 'Smart shapes: On' and 'Hold: Normal'.

12. THE INDEX MAP [P6]
- Open it from the bar's Index button, from the Graph chip on the Index tab, or with the 'index-map' action. It fills the screen (GC16) and is titled 'Index', with a Graph | List switch.
- What it shows:
  - Every page is a dot.
  - The open page has a double ring, and named pages are labelled.
  - Well-linked pages are solid; less-linked ones are half or quarter dithered.
  - Unnamed pages without links are small hollow dots clustered around their section's named page. Unlinked pages that come before any name sit in a 'Not linked yet' tray.
- Interaction:
  - Tap a dot: a card shows the name, 'p. 12 · 3 out · 2 in', and Open, Around it, Rename.
  - Tap the dot again to go there.
  - Drag with one finger to pan and pinch to zoom: rough DU previews while moving, one crisp GL16 when you let go.

13. SETTINGS > GESTURES [P4]
- The Settings bottom row reads KOReader | Controller | Gestures | Updates | Done.
- The sheet lists, in order:
  - 'Gestures: on (tap to change)';
  - Editing..., Tools..., Pages..., Index..., Menus..., Screen...;
  - Reset gestures;
  - Done.
- Each row inside a group reads 'Action: gesture', for example 'Pages view: 2 fingers down'.
- Tap a row and a card asks 'Do the gesture for Undo'. When Grimoire recognises it, the card shows '2-finger tap' large, with Use, Try again and Cancel.
  - If the gesture belonged to another action, the card first says 'Now for Redo. Use moves it here.'
  - A try Grimoire refuses says why, for example 'Put the fingers down together.' or 'The pen is near: move it away.'
- Hold a row for 0.6 s to clear it. Reset gestures brings back the built-in ones.
- It all works with controller shortcuts off.

14. WHEN THINGS GO WRONG
- If links.ini cannot be read, the bar says 'Links could not be read.' and New link says why instead of doing nothing.
- A gesture refused only because the pen was near shows 'Move the pen away, then swipe.' at most once every 10 minutes.
- In a notebook of 2000 pages and 4000 links, the bar, the card and following a link cost the same as anywhere else. The map opens on a quick placement and tidies itself once its background layout finishes.
plan.gestures:
ONE VOCABULARY, fixed (question 6). Nothing free-form.
- touch.2.up, touch.2.down, touch.2.left, touch.2.right, touch.2.tap.
- touch.3.*: the same five. Offered only when the step-1 device log, and InputCaps.touch_slots from a new EVIOCGABS(ABS_MT_SLOT) probe, show at least 3 contacts.
- touch.1.up, touch.1.down, touch.1.left, touch.1.right: one-finger swipes, recordable but never bound by default. They are recognised only when the finger started on the page (not on the panel or a sheet), did not become a link hold, and travelled at least 30 mm in at most 600 ms, within 30 degrees of an axis.
- pen.<Button|Button2|Eraser>.<tap|double|triple|hold|drag>: the pen plan's slots, recorded in the same sheet in P7. The 350 ms multi-tap gap is the owner's pen ruling.
- Edge swipes are not separate gestures. The edge band is only a rule for telling a swipe from a pan.
- Reserved, never recordable:
  - one-finger tap and hold (UI, links, the bar);
  - a two-finger spread or squeeze while pinch zoom is on;
  - a two-finger drag the view can follow (a pan).
- Names (EN / ES):
  - '2 fingers up' / '2 dedos arriba'
  - '2 fingers down' / '2 dedos abajo'
  - '2 fingers left' / '2 dedos izq.'
  - '2 fingers right' / '2 dedos der.'
  - '2-finger tap' / 'Toque con 2 dedos'
  - the same pattern for 3 fingers and 1 finger.
  Two-press rows use the short forms: '2 dedos izq. / 2 dedos der.' measures 1395 px, inside the 1470 px column.

BUILT-IN DEFAULTS. Never written to a file.
- touch.2.down = pages
- touch.2.up = links (the bar)
- touch.2.left = next-page and touch.2.right = previous-page (question 5). When a gesture moves past the last page it toasts 'This is the last page.' / 'Es la última página.' and never adds a page.
- pen.Button.triple = clear-page and pen.Button.hold = clear-page, as today.
- Two-finger and three-finger taps stay unbound. The sheet suggests them on a 'Try' line: 'Ideas: two-finger tap for Undo, three-finger tap for Redo.'
- MIRROR RULE: while a menu is in front, the mirror of that menu's own bound gesture closes it. The mirror has the same finger count with up and down, or left and right, swapped. So two fingers up close the Pages view, and two fingers down close the bar (back to the origin page). The menu's own gesture also closes it.

RECOGNIZER: src/touchgest.c/.h
Pure code in CORE_SRC, built and host-tested like pensync.c. input_evdev.c and sim_sdl.c both feed it contact frames.

Inputs per SYN_REPORT:
- the kernel CLOCK_MONOTONIC time;
- per contact: tracking id, logical x and y after calibration and rotation, tool, touch_major, pressure;
- pen context: prox, touching, left_ms, last contact point, and the hover point with its age, when the pensync hover mapping has been learned;
- view context, pushed by the editor whenever view_clamp, the sheets, the screen or the settings change:
  - scrolls_v = the view is taller than the screen AND pinch_zoom is on;
  - scrolls_h, the same for width;
  - zoom_ok, gestures_on, record, keyboard_open.

Cost: O(1) per frame, no allocation, signed 32-bit time differences.

1. ONE FINGER. Exactly today's stream: IN_TOUCH_DOWN at once, MOVE on change, UP at lift, with no added latency. The global 1 s pen window still applies to single fingers.

2. LANDING
- A second contact within 150 ms (provisional, set from the log): the first finger ends with the off-screen cancel (never a tap), IN_PINCH_BEGIN goes out with value 0, and the session can become a gesture.
- A second contact 150-400 ms after the first: zoom or pan only, never a swipe or tap.
- More than 400 ms later: a palm, suppressed (today's rule).
- A third contact within 250 ms makes three fingers.
- The finger count is fixed at the first of: any contact moving 3 mm; the end of the landing window; the first lift. A contact that lands later rejects the gesture, except during a committed zoom.

3. COMMIT (today's dead zone)
The session commits when the spread changes by 10% or more, or the midpoint travels at least 70 px. It is classified once, there:
- ZOOM if zoom_ok and spread_px >= 0.6 x trans.
- Otherwise TRANSLATE along the dominant axis. More than 30 degrees off axis is a PAN if either axis scrolls, else a reject ('Swipe in a straight line').
- A TRANSLATE is a PAN when the view scrolls on that AXIS (per axis, never per direction, so a drag that starts at a scroll limit never navigates by surprise) and the start midpoint is outside that direction's edge band. The bands are 25 mm (295 px) at the top for down and at the bottom for up, and 15 mm (177 px) at the sides.
- Otherwise it is a SWIPE candidate, and nothing moves on screen.
- Three fingers are never ZOOM or PAN.

4. EVENT CONTRACT
IN_PINCH_MOVE.value carries the class:
- 0 = legacy, the editor decides as today. The runner's 'pinch' and the simulator's mouse wheel push 0, so every existing pinch scenario keeps working.
- 1 = ZOOM: the editor skips its own 10%/70 px dead zone, since touchgest has committed, and re-anchors at the first classified move. This fixes the double dead zone.
- 2 = PAN: offsets only, with the zoom held at its commit value. This ends today's zoom wobble.
- 3 = SWIPE: the editor ignores the moves.
IN_PINCH_END comes first, then IN_GESTURE {value = gesture id, x, y = start midpoint, x2, y2 = end midpoint} in the same batch, so S->pinching is already clear when editor_shortcut checks it.
In record mode a rejection arrives as IN_GESTURE with a negative value, the reason code.

5. FIRING, at the first lift
- A SWIPE fires when all of these hold:
  - travel along the axis >= 20 mm (236 px);
  - off-axis travel <= tan 30 degrees of that;
  - each finger moved >= 12 mm, with cosine >= 0.8 to the midpoint's direction;
  - the largest finger travel is at most 2x the smallest;
  - the spread changed by 25% or less;
  - no more than 1000 ms from the first landing.
  Sliding back under 20 mm cancels it.
- A TAP: every contact lifts within 150 ms of the others, at most 300 ms from the first landing to the last lift, and no contact moves more than 5 mm.
- No multi-finger double taps in v1, so nothing ever waits. Pending timeouts, like the 3-finger landing window, resolve only when the last input batch drained the queue (App.input_drained).
- After a fire or a reject, every contact stays suppressed until all have lifted (today's T.suppressed), so a late finger never leaks a tap or a link follow.

6. RESTING CONTACTS (a grip thumb, the writing palm)
- A contact counts as resting if it stayed within 3 mm for 300 ms before the gesture's first finger, or if the panel flags it MT_TOOL_PALM.
- It is left out of the finger count and of the landing rule, provided every gesture finger is at least 40 mm from it.
- If it moves more than 3 mm during the gesture, the gesture is rejected ('Your hand moved: try again.').
- This replaces today's rule that any later finger is a late palm, for multi-finger gestures only.

7. PEN NEAR, staged (single fingers keep the global 1 s rule)
P2 ships the conservative rule. For a multi-finger gesture:
- pen touching: reject;
- pen in proximity: reject;
- pen gone less than 300 ms: reject;
- pen gone 300-1000 ms: accept when every finger is at least 40 mm from the pen's last contact point.
P4, after the step-1 log is read: also accept while the pen hovers, when the hover mapping is learned (hover_learn then runs on contact frames always, not only for Live view), the hover point is no older than 50 ms, and every finger is at least 60 mm from it.
Size guards, from the log: TOUCH_MAJOR above T_palm rejects (the guard only logs until the log is read); fingers closer than 8 mm or farther than 70 mm apart reject; a contact ever reported as tool 1 is never a finger.
A valid swipe refused only because of the pen toasts 'Move the pen away, then swipe.' / 'Aparta el lápiz y desliza.' at most once per 10 minutes.

8. INPUT FIXES, folded into the extraction (step 2)
- Pen arrival and the palm window end a finger with the off-screen cancel, never a real lift (input_evdev.c:477, 764).
- SYN_DROPPED resyncs every slot with EVIOCGMTSLOTS and suppresses until all lift (the pattern at 1627-1640).
- Kernel timestamps.
- input_pump also drains touch into touchgest, so a 1.2 s render no longer overflows the inferred 512-1024-event buffer.
- The device-scan busy flag counts every down contact.
- The pinch pair is chosen by landing order.
- When PINCH_BEGIN cancels a panel press, the button is restored with DU, not GL16.

DISPATCH
- IN_GESTURE gets a name in main.c's event_name (with its static assert), is dropped while asleep, is ignored while a book is being added (app.c:462), and counts as presence (app.c:464).
- On SCR_EDITOR, editor_gesture looks it up in gesturemap, applies the mirror rule, then calls editor_shortcut_at(a, action, x, y, SRC_TOUCH).
- So every existing gate holds: idle only; menu actions act through open menus; nothing acts through a keyboard; and all gestures are ignored while any keyboard is open.
- SRC_TOUCH and SRC_PEN never create a page from next-page.
- Gestures do not need Enable shortcuts. The master switch is settings.ini gestures (default 1).
- Elsewhere: the Pages view honours only the mirror close; the Library listens only in record mode.
- A one-time hint, the first time a two-finger vertical drag scrolls while 2-up or 2-down is bound: 'To open Pages or links here, start at the top or bottom edge.' / 'Para abrir Páginas o enlaces aquí, empieza en el borde de arriba o de abajo.'

THE GESTURES SHEET (Settings > Gestures, P4)
It is the Buttons sheet's code, parametrized by a BindKind descriptor {title, prompt, sources, text, learn, forget, reset}, not a copy.
- List: 'Gestures: on (tap to change)', Editing..., Tools..., Pages..., Index..., Menus..., Screen..., Reset gestures, Done. That is 9 rows, under the 12-row sideways limit.
- Group rows read 'Action: touch gesture, pen gesture' or 'Action: none'. Hold-eraser and the gestures switch are left out.
- RECORDING
  - Tap a row. touchgest goes into record mode: no zoom or pan side effects, every class and every rejection reported, with the same constants as at runtime, so whatever records will also fire. A unit test checks they stay the same.
  - A card opens (1400 wide):
    - title 'Do the gesture for %s' / 'Haz el gesto para %s';
    - body 'Swipe or tap with two fingers, or use the pen's button.';
    - footer 'When the page can scroll, swipe from the edge.' / 'Si la página se desplaza, desliza desde el borde.'
  - Rejections update one line with a GL16 of that line only:
    - 'The pen is near: move it away.' / 'El lápiz está cerca: apártalo.'
    - 'Put the fingers down together.' / 'Apoya los dedos a la vez.'
    - 'Swipe in a straight line.' / 'Desliza en línea recta.'
    - 'Swipe farther.' / 'Desliza más lejos.'
    - 'Move both fingers the same way.' / 'Mueve los dos dedos igual.'
    - 'Your hand moved: try again.' / 'La mano se movió: inténtalo otra vez.'
    - 'Two fingers spreading is kept for zoom.' / 'Separar dos dedos es para el zoom.'
    - 'One finger is kept for taps and links.' / 'Un dedo es para tocar y enlaces.'
  - A recognised gesture shows its name at 64 px with Use / Try again / Cancel ('Usar' / 'Otra vez' / 'Cancelar'). If it belongs to another action, the card first says 'Now for %s. Use moves it here.', and Use then toasts 'That gesture is no longer for %s.'
  - gestures.ini is written atomically, and the map changes only after the write succeeds.
  - 10 s with no attempt leaves the row as it was. A second tap on the row stops recording. A 0.6 s hold clears the row (a cleared default is written as '=nothing'). Reset deletes gestures.ini.
- BINDING RULE, the same for both sheets: per source, a binding does one action, and an action has at most one binding per source (touch, pen, pad). Keys keep shortcuts.ini's many-to-one. Built-in duplicates stay legal.

SIMULATOR AND RUNNER
- Window: Shift + right-drag = two fingers 25 mm apart moving together; Alt + right-drag = three fingers; Ctrl + right-click = a two-finger tap. The wheel stays the pinch (value 0).
- Runner, through touchgest on a virtual clock:
  - 'finger ID down|move|up X Y [MAJOR] [TOOL]', grouped into a frame until 'frame [MS]' (default 13 ms);
  - 'swipe N X Y DX DY [STEPS] [SEP] [LANDGAP]';
  - 'tapn N X Y [SEP] [MS]';
  - 'pen hover' and 'pen leave' drive the pen context.
  The legacy 'tap', 'touch', 'drag touch' and 'pinch' still push events directly.
- Probes: touch.gesture, touch.reject, touch.class, touch.contacts, touch.suppressed, gestures.ACTION, library.gestures_group, library.gestures.learning.
plan.hotbar:
WHAT IT IS
'Links' / 'Enlaces': the Index entries this page links to.
- In code it is src/linkbar.c. The editor hosts it like dispmenu, and linkbar_pointer returns LB_* results (PEEK, COMMIT, CANCEL, BACK, NEW_LINK, GOTO, EYE, INDEX, CARD) that the editor acts on.
- It is a MENU action ('links'), so it joins sheet_open, front_menu, menu_action, close_front and open_menu (editor.c:1374-1376, 1906-1965). Its own action closes it, another menu's action swaps, and Close menu closes it.
- While it is up, every other shortcut is refused (editor.c:2010), so nothing (no undo, no page turn) happens behind a peek.
- Opening it disarms link mode.

CONTENT (question 1 decides grouped versus per-link; grouped is the default)
One entry per distinct target among the page's live links: stored areas, plus beta.5 links whose ink still exists.
- Order: reading order of each entry's first area. Area tops within 10 mm count as one line, read left to right.
- Entries are numbered 1..n, and the eye tags every area with its entry's number.
- Labels:
  - a named target: its Index name, bold 44 px, cut with font_draw_left_name;
  - an unnamed page: 'Page 20', regular weight;
  - a link to the Index: the list glyph and 'The Index';
  - a deleted page or an unknown target: 'Page not here', 50% dithered. A tap toasts 'That link's page is not in this notebook.'; a long press offers Delete;
  - a legacy link with no area and no ink is not listed (dormant, as today).
- Right column: 'p. 12' at 34 px, and '×2' on a second line when two links on this page go to the same entry.
- Backlinks are not a list section. From P6 the header carries a small chip, '%d pages link here' / '%d páginas enlazan aquí', that opens the Index map around this page. It is hidden when the count is 0.

LAYOUT, UPRIGHT (1860 x 2480)
The card is at x 20, 1820 wide, its bottom 20 px above the screen edge. From the top:
- 16 px padding;
- a 36 px grip strip with a 160 x 8 px bar;
- a 100 px header:
  - origin: the title 'Links on this page (%d)' / 'Enlaces de esta página (%d)' with an X (118 x 100) at the right. When there are more than 6 entries, a pager ‹ 1/3 › (two 118 x 100 buttons) sits left of the X;
  - peek: a back chip '‹ Page 3' (at most 380 px), then 'Showing %s. Tap the page to stay.' / 'Mostrando %s. Toca la página para quedarte.' (truncated), then the X;

LAYOUT, SIDEWAYS (2480 x 1860)
The card is 2440 wide, with 3 columns of 784 x 124 (3 x 784 + 2 x 24 = 2400 = 2440 - 40), at most 2 rows (6 per screen). Tool buttons are 585 x 140. Height 456 or 596 px, at most 32% of 1860.

The card draws above the panel and every editor sheet. After compose resets a->toast_floor, the card sets it to its own top (editor.c:676).

TOOL ROW
- Go to / Ir a (magnifier F0349)
- New link / Nuevo enlace (link-plus F0339)

- Index / Índice (three bubbles F05E3)
TRANSLATORS width note: 'about 400 px at 34 px caps'.

OPENING
- Two fingers up (default), the Links panel button (question 7), or the 'links' action.
- The card is composed into App.screen and its rect GL16'd: about 50-90 ms of CPU plus 271 ms.
- On a read-only page the bar opens for browsing, with New link drawn disabled; a tap on it toasts 'This page is read-only.'
- If links.ini is unreadable: 'Links could not be read.' New link and Areas are disabled, and New link toasts the reason when tapped.

TAP AN ENTRY: PEEK
1. app_press_feedback inverts the chip at once (DU).
2. A peek is a display state only. S->index, S->page, the page's history and link hit tests all stay on the origin until a commit, so autosave, undo or a link tap can never act on the peeked page.
3. The peek canvas comes from a 3-entry LRU of rendered canvases (the origin pinned, plus two targets). On a miss it renders with the pumped page reader and page_render (pumped).
4. compose blits the peek canvas at the target's default view instead of page_canvas, and only the page area above the card is sent as GL16. No GC16.
5. The selected chip keeps an 8 px frame. The header switches to the peek state, and the panel's page chip shows the peeked number.
6. Peeks never set nb.last_page or info_dirty and never write thumbnails.
7. Tapping the selected entry again commits, the same as tapping the page.
8. An entry for The Index commits, then opens the Index list (FULL).

COMMIT (STAY)
- FINGER outside the card, the panel included: the touch becomes OWN_MODAL. The commit happens on LIFT within the 30 px slop. If a second finger lands first, the pending commit is cancelled and the touch becomes a gesture. This fixes the trap in which the first finger of a two-finger close swipe committed and the gesture then opened Pages.
- PEN outside: commits on pen down, and the stroke is swallowed until pen up. That keeps the next stroke on MTK pen mode, since the closing refresh is not raced.
- Commit makes the peeked page current: index, page_at, the peek canvas swapped into page_canvas. It sets last_page and info_dirty, writes the origin's thumbnail if needed, closes the card and sends one REFRESH_FULL (GC16), which clears the peeks' ghosts.
- With no peek, the tap outside only closes, with a GL16 of the card rect, and is swallowed.
- The origin goes on the back list. Committing a page reached through Back pops the list instead, as a browser's Back does.

CANCEL (BACK TO THE ORIGIN)
- Triggered by: X; the 'links' action or the Links button again; two fingers down (the mirror); a one-finger drag of 15 mm or more down that starts on the grip or header; Close menu; the Back key.
- If peeking: the origin canvas is swapped back at the zoom and offset it had. Then compose_all with REFRESH_UI, or REFRESH_FULL after 3 or more peeks, because GL16 ghosting builds up.
- Otherwise: a GL16 of the card rect.

BACK CHIP
- While peeking: shows the origin again (canvas swap, GL16 of the page area). The bar stays.
- When not peeking and the back list is not empty: 'Back to Chapter 1' peeks the top of the back list.

ACTS ON THE SHOWN PAGE, SO IT COMMITS FIRST
- New link: commit, then link mode on that page. The bar folds into the link-mode strip and comes back afterwards with the new entry.
- Go to: commit, then the Find sheet.
- Index: commit, then the Index map (P6), or the Pages view's Index tab before P6.
- Another menu's button or key: commit, then swap.

LONG PRESS AN ENTRY (600 ms within the slop)
- If peeking, first return to the origin with a GL16, because the links live there.
- Then the link card opens above the card, aligned with the chip's column. The entry's areas get the heavy dotted border (four DU strips each).
- The card's rows are those of the page's card. For a ×N entry they read 'Delete %d links' and 'Change where they go', with the line 'To change one, hold it on the page.' / 'Para cambiar uno, mantenlo pulsado en la página.' Delete removes all N as one ACT_LINK group step.
- Before P3 the long press opens today's retarget path (pagesview_pick).

AREAS: toggles settings.link_areas and saves. A GL16 of the button, plus a GL16 of the union of the visible areas, flushed separately when they are far apart. No toast; the first time only, hints bit 2.

PAGER: ‹ and › redraw the chip grid only, with a GL16.

INSTANT JUMPS
- Canvas LRU: up to 3 x 4.6 MB (5.3 MB at 1986 x 2648). The key is page id + the page's edit generation + paper generation + page size. A peek swaps structs, never memcpys. The cache is freed when the card closes, and an allocation failure shrinks it to nothing: slower peeks, the same pixels.
- Prefetch runs in editor_tick only when App.input_drained and no owner holds the pointer:
  - the targets of the visible entries, then the top of the back list;
  - one 160-row render band per tick;
  - pages not in memory load through the new pumped page reader (step 10);
  - it stops at the first contact.

CHECKLIST FOR EVERY NEW SURFACE (bar, link card, link-mode strip, Link to..., Find, Index map, record card)
- joins sheet_open, front_menu, menu_action, close_front and open_menu;
- sets toast_floor after compose;
- swallows its tap outside on lift (pen on down);
- never draws while the pen is down;

plan.link_areas:
MODEL (ruling 1)
- A link is (page id, seed, target, area). The area is an axis-aligned rectangle in page px at the notebook's page size, stored in links.ini on an area. line next to the unchanged link. line.
- The area is invisible. It never goes into page_canvas, thumbnails, the share page, the PDF page image or the sleep image. Only overlays in App.screen show it: the eye, the dashed lasso while drawing, the dotted rectangle until a target is picked, and the heavy border of a long press.
- The seed stays the link's id. nav_new_seed keeps it unique per page and already makes new ink avoid link seeds.
- A visible border is the owner's own ink (smart shapes or freehand), with its own seed, and is never part of the link. Erasing it keeps the link; deleting the link keeps it.
- The trick of giving a border the link's seed is deliberately not used: it would bring back the dependence on ink and the precise-eraser quirk.

HIT TEST
- Each link's box is its area. An unmigrated legacy link uses the point box of its ink strokes instead, erase strokes ignored.
- The box is padded to at least 7 mm a side around its centre (NAV_LINK_MIN_MM).
- The SMALLEST padded box under the finger wins; a tie goes to the lower seed. This replaces 'last stroke wins', so nested links behave and no creation order is stored.
- The editor caches the open page's boxes (at most 64, with entry numbers). The cache is rebuilt on page change, link edits and migration. While legacy links remain on the page, it is also rebuilt on draw_end, erase_end, undo/redo and clear.
- nav_link_areas also prefers areas, so the PDF's /Link annotations (export.c:94-117) follow without any change to export. Links to the Index stay dropped from the PDF, as today.

MAKING ONE (P3)
1. ARM from the bar's New link, the 'add-link' action or the Index tab's Add a link. A refusal says why:
   - read-only: the read-only toast;
   - links.ini unreadable: 'Links could not be read in this notebook.';
   - 64 links on the page: 'This page has 64 links: delete one to add another.'
2. STRIP: 1820 x 130 at the bottom, GL16: 'Draw around what links.' / 'Rodea lo que enlaza.' with Cancel (260 x 100). Pressing add-link again, Close menu, Cancel, a page change or leaving the editor disarms it, and nothing is written.
3. LASSO: the next pen contact is OWN_LASSO, whatever the tool, the eraser end included, and smart shapes never apply.
   - Its points (page px, decimated to at most 4096) draw a 4 px black dashed line (12 on, 8 off) as an overlay layer that compose redraws.
   - Each batch of segments goes out as REFRESH_FAST under display_live_ink(true).
   - Nothing touches page_canvas, the page or history, so no tile backup is needed.
4. LIFT:
   - Under 5 mm both ways (LINK_BOX_MIN_MM): the dashes are recomposed away, the toast is 'Too small for a link: draw around what links.' / 'Demasiado pequeño para un enlace: rodea lo que enlaza.', and the mode stays.
   - Otherwise the area is the points' box, clamped to the page. One REFRESH_UI of the union swaps the dashes for a dotted rectangle (3 px dashes, white halo).
5. LINK TO... (the bar's frame in pick mode)
   - Title: 'Where does the link go?' / '¿Adónde va el enlace?'
   - It docks at the TOP (y 20) when the area's centre is in the lower 45% of the screen, otherwise at the bottom.
   - Chips: New page... / Página nueva..., The Index / El índice, up to 4 Recent targets (this session's link targets and the last visited pages, this page left out), then the Index entries in Index order, paged.
   - Tool row: Search (opens Find in PICK mode; kbhost docks the keyboard on the side away from the area), Choose from the pages... (today's Pages-view picker, the only part of picking mode that is kept), Cancel.
6. PICK:
   - nav_link_set plus the area, then nav_save_links. On failure, nav_load rolls back and the toast is 'Could not save the link.'
   - On success, one ACT_LINK step and the toast 'Linked to %s.' / 'Enlazado con %s.' The first time it adds 'Tap it with a finger to go there; hold it for more.' (hints bit 1).
   - The dotted rectangle ends at the pick (unless the eye is on). Ruling 1 shows areas only while a link is made.
   - If the flow started from the bar, the bar comes back.
7. NEW PAGE...: kbhost asks 'Name the new page' / 'Nombre de la página nueva' over the page. Done does store_add_page at npages (the end), then nav_set_name; an empty name leaves the page unnamed. Then the link, and the toast 'Linked to the new page %d.' The editor stays on the origin. Cancel adds no page and returns to Link to....
8. CANCEL at any point: 'No link made.' / 'No se hizo ningún enlace.' Nothing to undo.

THE EYE (P2; settings.ini link_areas, default 0, remembered; action 'link-areas')
- In compose(r), after the page blit and before the panel, for every cached box that meets r:
  - the HIT box, so what the eye promises is what a finger hits;
  - a 4 px black dashed outline (16 on, 12 off) on a 2 px white halo;
  - a 52 x 52 white tag with a 3 px frame and the entry number in 34 px bold, at the top-left corner, kept inside the screen.
- 1-bit only, so DU and GL16 look alike and inversion keeps it distinct.
- At most 64 rect tests per compose, and the live-ink composes reuse the cache.
- In P2 the boxes come from the legacy ink fallback; from P3 they are stored areas.

LONG PRESS (ruling 2, P3)
- At 600 ms within the 30 px slop, the heavy border goes around the box inflated 8 px:
  - 5 px black dashes (20 on, 14 off) on a 3 px white halo on both sides;
  - solid 24 px corner Ls.
  Only the four strips go out by DU, with their own app_flush, so the gray ink inside is not dithered. The card follows by GL16. When the card closes, card and strips are GL16'd.
- Card: 780 x 666.
  - Title row (110): target name in 44 px bold plus 'p. 12' at 34 px.
  - Four 118 px rows with 12 px gaps:
    - Rename in the Index / Renombrar en el índice. For an unnamed page: 'Add page %d to the Index...' / 'Añadir la página %d al índice...'. Disabled for The Index, an unknown target, or an unwritable nav.ini.
    - Change where it goes... / Cambiar a dónde lleva...
    - Redraw the area / Volver a dibujar la zona
    - Delete link / Borrar enlace
  - TRANSLATORS width: 'about 700 px at 44 px'.
- PLACEMENT: 24 px to the right of the box if it fits within a 20 px margin; else left; else below; else above. It is clamped to the screen, never covers the box when any placement avoids it, and slides horizontally to avoid the panel.
- Rename: kbhost over the page, titled 'Name in the Index'. Done calls nav_set_name(target pid) plus nav_save, with the pid parametrised (the pattern at editor.c:1643-1656), and restores the old name on failure. Naming an unnamed page toasts 'Page %d is in the Index as %s.' so the new section start is no surprise.
- Change where it goes: Link to... with the current target marked, then an ACT_LINK retarget.
- Redraw the area: link mode for this link ('Draw the link's new area'); the new box replaces the old one as an ACT_LINK step.
- Delete link: nav_link_remove, a save and an ACT_LINK step. Toast 'Link deleted. Undo brings it back.'
- A tap outside closes the card and is swallowed (OWN_MODAL, on lift). Close menu closes it.
- The Pages view's hold path (link_hold, PG_UNLINK, PG_TO_INDEX) is retired in P3.

UNDO
- ACT_LINK lives in the page's history (memory only): {pid, seed, n, records[n] of before {exists, target, area} and after {...}}. n > 1 is the ×N group delete or retarget.
- Undo and redo re-apply the records and save links.ini.
- If the save fails: nav_load restores what is on disk, the step is explicitly dropped from the stack it was just moved to (new history_drop_last_redo / _undo), and the toast is 'Could not save the links: that change was not undone.' This fixes the history_undo behaviour verified at history.c:177.
- Redo after the target page was deleted does nothing.

COPY PAGE: copies the page's links (same seeds, areas and targets) to the copy's pid. Any legacy link is migrated first, since the source page is loaded.

MIGRATING THE OWNER'S BETA.5 LINKS (ruling 1)
- A link. line with no area. line is LEGACY. It keeps working exactly as today, through the ink-box fallback, in the editor, the bar, the eye and the PDF.
- ON PAGE LOAD (page_at): each legacy link of that page whose ink exists gets an area = the UNPADDED point box of its ink strokes (never the 7 mm grown box), erase strokes ignored, rounded outward to whole px. The links are marked dirty.
- IDLE: after a notebook opens with legacy lines, editor_tick handles one such page per idle tick (input drained, no owner). Pages in memory are used directly; others are read with the pumped page reader. The main.longest_unpumped_ms probe must stay under 100 ms.
- FLUSH: save_page never writes links.ini (it saves only a dirty page, editor.c:751), so nav_save_links runs explicitly whenever links_dirty: on leaving a page, in the 2 s idle autosave tick, at notebook close and at editor_leave.
- The lasso ink stays as ordinary ink, and its seed stays reserved.
- A lasso hidden by the precise eraser or white ink still has its stroke, so it migrates to a working area that the eye shows. The silent death at compaction is gone.
- A legacy link with no ink stays dormant and is pruned only with its page.
- If links.ini is unwritable, nothing migrates and the fallback keeps working.
plan.smart_shapes:
TRIGGER
- Draw, then hold the nib still within 1.0 screen mm (11.8 px) for shape_hold_ms. The default is 550; the choices are Quick 400, Normal 550 and Slow 900.
- draw_sample keeps the anchor in O(1): a sample more than 1 mm from the anchor moves it and resets its kernel time.
- editor_tick (at least every 30 ms, pen down too) checks the hold by wall time, never by sample spacing, because a still relayed pen may send nothing. It checks only when App.input_drained, so a backlog is never mistaken for stillness.
- It evaluates once per still period.
- It applies to ink strokes of all nine pens, the highlighter and the side button's highlighter included. It never applies to erase strokes, white ink, the precise or whole-stroke eraser, read-only pages, or the link lasso.

RECOGNIZER: src/shape.c, pure and geometric (no timing features, because runner batches share one time). About 0.12 ms on the Kindle. It resamples at the bbox diagonal / 40. Sizes are in screen mm: page px = mm x dpi / 25.4 / zoom.
- LINE: chord/path >= 0.97; max offset <= max(4% of the length, 1 mm) + 0.5 mm; at least 12 mm long. Snaps to 0, 45, 90 or 135 degrees within 4 degrees.
- CLOSED (a prerequisite for the shapes below):
  - the end gap is at most 22% of the diagonal;
  - winding around the centroid is 1.7-2.6 pi;
  - total absolute turning is at most 1.6 x the winding + 0.6 pi, which rejects scribbles;
  - at least 10 mm across and 4 mm thick.
- RECTANGLE / SQUARE / QUAD: ShortStraw finds 4 segments, each with chord/path >= 0.93. Every angle within 15 degrees of 90 makes a rectangle: axis-aligned within 5 degrees, a square when the sides are within 10%. Otherwise a straight-edged quad, which is how diamonds come out.
- TRIANGLE: 3 segments. Equilateral or right-angled snaps within 7 degrees.
- ELLIPSE / CIRCLE: a PCA frame plus a least-squares fit. RMS radial error at most 6% of the minor axis, maximum at most 20%. A circle when the axis ratio is >= 0.88; axis-aligned within 6 degrees.
- PAPER-AWARE (v1, no setting): on Dot grid and Graph paper, line ends and rectangle corners snap to the 5 mm grid within 1 mm. On ruled papers a near-horizontal line snaps exactly horizontal.
- v1.5 (step 22, shipped only if the corpus gate passes): single-stroke ARROW (a shaft, then one or two barbs at 20-70 degrees, each 15-45% of the shaft), open POLYLINE with 90-degree snaps, and ARC.

CONFIDENCE AND ACCIDENT DEFENCES, strongest first
1. A hold only previews. Moving on restores your line, and the stroke continues untouched.
2. Gates that can say no: size in screen mm, closure, winding, the scribble budget, fit residuals. On the owner's 47 real strokes, a hold-only trigger like Amazon's would fire 21 times; these gates gave no preview at written size.
3. Writing-burst gate: a stroke started within 600 ms and 8 mm of the last lift needs tolerances 0.7x as wide and a 1.5x hold.
4. One Undo removes the shape.
5. A panel toggle plus an adjustable hold, both assignable: the two things Amazon's users asked for.
6. Never on erasers, white ink or the lasso.

PREVIEW (the simple path, live equals re-render by construction)
1. At an accepted hold, the region = union(raw bbox, shape bbox), padded by the brush's max radius + 2.
2. Copy that region of page_canvas (the with-raw pixels).
3. draw_page(region) renders the page without the stroke in progress. The raw stroke is not page_add'ed until lift. This is pumped every 64 rows.
4. Stamp the snapped stroke with stroke_brush_begin and brush_add, calling work_pump every 8 points.
5. show(region, REFRESH_FAST): one DU frame, and pen mode is kept.
- Moving more than 1.5 mm from the anchor (hysteresis over the 1.0 mm hold radius) puts the saved copy back (a memcpy) with one DU frame. The raw BrushState was never touched.
- Lift or LEAVE: page_add(shape) with ONE history_push_add. The raw stroke is never added. No redraw; the region joins S->settle for the usual GL16.
- Holding longer does nothing more.
- No GL16 and no toast while the pen is down.
- If the region copy cannot be allocated, that stroke gets no preview.
- An under-ink tile backup comes later only if the shape-log shows region renders over about 300 ms on the owner's pages.

STORAGE
The snapped stroke is an ordinary Stroke: the raw stroke's tool id (0-9), ToolParams snapshot, ext bytes, tip variant and seed. Only the points differ:
- polygons: vertices at the intersections of the least-squares edge lines, plus a point every 2 mm;
- ellipses: N = clamp(ceil(2 pi / acos(1 - 0.25 px / r)), 24, 720) vertices;
- the stroke starts nearest the user's first point, runs in the user's direction, and closed shapes close exactly;
- pressure is the median of the middle 80% of samples by arc length; tilt is the median; t_ms is interpolated by arc length.
No format change and no ext flag. Older versions draw it as the pen stroke it is.

UNDO: one pen-down is one moment, so one Undo removes the shape. This is the owner's documented undo rule, and it is decided here, not asked.

shape-last ('Shape the last stroke' / 'Dar forma al último trazo')
- Runs all the gates, but no hold, on the page's newest ink stroke when the top undo step is that stroke's ACT_ADD.
- It makes one ACT_REPLACE step (count 2: raw out, shape in), so Undo brings the freehand stroke back. Then draw_page(union), pumped, and REFRESH_UI.
- Otherwise it toasts 'No shape in the last stroke.' / 'El último trazo no es una forma.'
- It gives a zero-accident way in for writers who turn the hold off.

TOGGLE
- Panel: P_SHAPES, a new button directly under the eraser, in the pen-behaviour group.
  - On: the filled glyph F0831 on a plain button. Off: the outline glyph F0832 with a 4 px diagonal slash (canvas_slash).
  - NEVER inverted: on this panel, inverted means the current tool (editor.c tool_style).
- Tap: settings.shapes flips, then settings_save and a GL16 of the button. Toasts:
  - 'Smart shapes on. Hold the pen still at the end of a shape.' / 'Formas inteligentes activadas. Mantén el lápiz quieto al final de una forma.'
  - 'Smart shapes off.' / 'Formas inteligentes desactivadas.'
- Tool picker: a labelled row under the ink row with two 520 px chips, 'Smart shapes: On' and 'Hold: Normal', so the icon is explained where there is room for words.
- Actions: 'shapes' (TOGGLE), 'shape-hold' (CYCLE; toast 'Shape hold: Normal (0.55 s)'), 'shape-last'.
- One-time tip after the first snap (hints bit 5): 'Shape made. Undo takes it away; the panel's shapes button turns this off.'

DEVICE TUNING: an empty grimoire/shape-log file logs each hold's features and decision: size in mm, winding, residuals, corners, kind or reason, and ms taken. It never logs coordinates. One evening of the owner's writing then sets the final thresholds.
plan.graph_view:
NAME AND ENTRY
- One Index destination. The view is titled 'Index' / 'Índice', with a Graph | List switch. List goes to the Pages view's Index tab (the existing list), whose header gains a Graph button.
- Open it from the bar's Index button, from that Graph button, or with the new 'index-map' action ('Index map' / 'Mapa del índice' in the Buttons and Gestures sheets).
- The 'index' action keeps its 1.2.0 meaning: the list. A link to The Index still opens the list.
- Hosting: src/mapview.c, full screen, like the Pages view, but drawn from its own offscreen canvas (screen size, 4.6 MB, freed on close). compose only blits it, so settles and toasts never re-render edges.
- It joins the sheet family and its checklist.
- Open and close are GC16.

DATA (no page loads)
- Built from nav.ini, links.ini and nb->page_ids in one O(n + e) pass, with a pid-to-index open-addressing table (4096 slots).
- Edges: links between pages, deduplicated per unordered pair, with direction bits and multiplicity.
- Links to The Index: a 16 px lozenge badge at the source dot's upper right, not edges, because an Index hub makes a hairball.
- Degree = the number of distinct linked neighbours.

NODES: every page is a dot, in three bands.
1. FORCE NODES: named pages, pages with any link, and the open page. Only these enter the force layout.
2. SATELLITES: unnamed pages with no links that have a named page before them. They are small hollow dots placed deterministically on phyllotaxis rings around their section's named page (nav_section_of) after the layout. They are never in the forces, so a 2000-page notebook costs no more than its linked part. When a section has more than 60 satellites, 60 are drawn plus a '+N' label; zooming to 2x or more shows them all.
3. TRAY: unnamed, unlinked pages before the first named page sit in a 'Not linked yet (%d)' / 'Aún sin enlaces (%d)' tray: below the graph upright, right of it sideways, at a 40 px pitch, in notebook order. With more than 200 it collapses to 'Not linked yet: %d pages. Show'.

LOOK (1-bit-safe marks, so DU previews match GL16 settles and inversion keeps them distinct)
- Fill by degree, getting progressively lighter as the owner asked:
  - 0: a hollow 3 px ring;
  - 1: a 25% Bayer dither (4x4 on 2x2-px cells) inside a ring;
  - 2-3: a 50% dither;
  - 4 or more: solid.
- Radius at fit = 14 + 16 x ln(1 + d) / ln(1 + dmax) px (14-30). Unnamed force nodes are drawn at 0.75x and satellites at 6 px.
- A named orphan (in the Index, linked by nothing) is hollow but labelled: an entry nothing links to yet.
- Open page: a concentric double ring 6 px apart. Selected: an 8 px ring, its edges at 5 px, outgoing edges solid and incoming dashed, so direction reads without arrowheads; its label becomes an inverted chip.
- Edges: 2.5 px anti-aliased lines (the row-span canvas_line_aa), plus 1 px per extra link up to 5 px, drawn under white knockout discs (r + 4).
- Labels: named pages in bold 34 px, at most 320 px wide (font_draw_left_name), on a white knockout box.
  - Placed greedily by priority: selected, open page, neighbours, then named pages by degree.
  - 4 candidate spots each, tested against placed labels and dots; a label that collides is skipped until zoomed.
  - 'p. N' labels for unnamed pages appear only at 2x zoom or in Around mode.

LAYOUT: src/graph.c, pure, in CORE_SRC
- SEED: Navi's place_disk. BFS shells grow from each component's top-degree hub, with rings sorted by parent angle and components packed outward. Jitter is deterministic, seeded by a hash of the page id, never its index.
- RELAX: about 300 Barnes-Hut steps (theta 0.9) with Navi's constants: REPULSION 16000, SPRING_K 0.055, SPRING_L 110, GRAVITY 0.02, DAMPING 0.9.
- WHERE IT RUNS:
  - up to 300 force nodes: in-process, with a work_pump callback every 2 steps (about 0.25 s on the Kindle);
  - more, or Tidy up: a niced bgjob child writes graph.ini atomically while the view shows the O(n + e) seed. The result is swapped in with one GL16 only while the map is open and idle (no input for 500 ms). 2000 force nodes with 4000 links take about 3.4 s in the child.
- INCREMENTAL: a new force node goes at its placed neighbours' centroid plus one rest length (or beside its section head), then 40 steps run over its 2-hop neighbourhood with everything else fixed (under 10 ms). A full relayout runs only when more than 10% of the nodes changed, or on Tidy up.
- Nothing moves between visits.
- Floats differ between arm64 and armv7, so positions persist in graph.ini and tests assert invariants, never coordinates.

SCREEN
- Upright header, 190 px:
  - Back (150 x 150);
  - the title 'Index' with Graph | List;
  - an 'All | Around' segment ('Todas | Alrededor', 2 x 300);
  - Fit.
- Bottom row, 170 px:
  - − and + (220 x 140);
  - 'Unlinked: Show / Hide' ('Sin enlaces: Mostrar / Ocultar'), the satellites and the tray;
  - 'Tidy up' / 'Ordenar', shown once positions exist.
- Selecting a dot replaces the bottom row with a 320 px card:
  - the name at 64 px;
  - 'Page 12. Links to 3, linked from 2.' / 'Página 12. Enlaza a 3, enlazada desde 2.';
  - Open, Around it, Rename (Rename uses kbhost over the map).
- Sideways: the same, with the tray on the right.

INTERACTION
- Tap a dot: the nearest within max(r x zoom, 59 px = 5 mm), by the view's own hit test (HitList holds only 128 entries). GL16 of the old and new selection plus the card.
- Tap the selected dot again, or Open: go_to_page (GC16), close the map, and push the origin on the back list.
- Tap empty space: deselect.
- One-finger or pen drag: pan. An offset blit is presented by DU at most every 180 ms; at release, a pumped re-render and one GL16.
- Pinch: zoom 0.25x-6x, with a nearest-neighbour scaled DU preview, then GL16. − and + step by 1.5x. Fit resets.
- Around: a radial ring layout (Navi's positions_radial). The centre page sits in the middle, depth 1 on one ring, depth 2 on an outer ring, angle-sorted by parent; only members are drawn. Instant and deterministic.
- Default view: All, centred on the open page at a zoom that fits its 2-step neighbourhood, or fits everything if that keeps dots at least 10 px.
- The last mode and the Unlinked choice are remembered per notebook in graph.ini.
- Back or Close menu returns to the page; 'pages' swaps to the Pages view.

PERFORMANCE
- Culled to the viewport. Drawing order: edges, knockouts, dots, labels. work_pump every 64 edges.
- About 50-70 ms on the Kindle for 100 nodes. Worst case, 2000 force nodes and 4000 edges at fit: 1-2 s, pumped, shown behind the seed frame.
- If the 4.6 MB offscreen canvas cannot be allocated: 'Not enough memory for the map.' and the List opens instead.

plan.data_and_formats:
THE .qpg FORMAT NEVER CHANGES
No header bump, no tool id >= 10, no ext flag, no chunk holding page coordinates. Snapped shapes are ordinary strokes. Areas, overlays, the bar, the card and the map are never in pages.

links.ini (2.0.0-beta.5, unreleased, so free to change)
  # Grimoire: links on pages
  link.12=0a1b2c3d,p7
  area.12=0a1b2c3d,410,1220,380,140
- link.<pid>=<seed>,<target>: byte for byte today's grammar. The target is index or p<pid>, 1-15 bytes from '!' to '~'.
- area.<pid>=<seed>,<x>,<y>,<w>,<h>: decimal page px at store_notebook_page_size. 0 <= x, y; 1 <= w, h; x + w and y + h <= 6000.
  - The last line for a pid+seed wins.
  - An area line with no matching link line is dropped at the next save and logged.
  - A malformed area line is carried verbatim, and its link falls back to the ink box.
  - After a page-size change an area is clamped; one left empty means no area.
- Links with an area use it; links without one use their ink box (the beta.5 rule).
- Size: a worst-case pair of lines is about 63 B, so 4000 links take about 252 KB plus up to 16 KiB of carried lines. links.ini therefore gets its own cap, NAV_LINKS_FILE_MAX = 512 KiB. nav.ini keeps 256 KiB. NAV_LINKS_MAX 4000 and NAV_LINKS_PER_PAGE 64 are unchanged.
- The device's f9d13f5 build on the new file:
  - it reads every link. line, and ink links keep working there because migration never removes ink;
  - it carries area. lines as unknown lines up to 16 KiB (about 430 links);
  - past that, or past 256 KiB, it refuses the file: links are read-only there and the file is never overwritten.
  - 1.2.0 to beta.4 never read links.ini.
- Writes stay whole and atomic, and an unreadable file is never overwritten.

gestures.ini (new, in root/ beside shortcuts.ini and controller.ini; absorbs the pen plan's unreleased pen.ini)
  # Grimoire: gestures (Settings > Gestures). Built in unless a line says otherwise:
  # touch.2.down=pages, touch.2.up=links, touch.2.left=next-page, touch.2.right=previous-page, pen.Button.triple=clear-page, pen.Button.hold=clear-page
  touch.2.tap=undo
  touch.2.left=nothing
  pen.Button.double=links
- Grammar: shortcuts.ini's. '#' and ';' comments, trimmed key=value, a later duplicate wins, case-insensitive.
- Keys: touch.<1|2|3>.<up|down|left|right|tap> (touch.1.tap is refused) and pen.<Button|Button2|Eraser>.<tap|double|triple|hold|drag>.
- Values: an action name, nothing, or pan|zoom in a drag slot.
- OVERLAY MODEL: built-in defaults are never written; a line overrides one, and '=nothing' switches one off. Defaults added later still reach the owner. Only slots that were set are written; when none are left the file is removed. Reset deletes it.
- Reads are bounded at 64 KiB through shortcuts.c's factored bounded reader.
  - A malformed line is refused and counted, and toasted when the sheet opens.
  - A well-formed line this version cannot use is kept verbatim, up to 2 KiB, and written back.
  - A file that does not read runs on the built-in defaults, is never overwritten, and the sheet offers Reset.
- It is read in app_init, by the Controller sheet's Reload, and each time the Gestures sheet opens.
- It cannot live in settings.ini: test_probe.c:29-39 and store.c reserve dotted pen. and touch. keys.

graph.ini (new, per notebook folder; a CACHE)
  # Grimoire: the Index map's layout (a cache: deleting it loses nothing)
  gen=5f3a9c21
  mode=all
  unlinked=show
  pos.12=-310,442
- gen is FNV-1a 32 of the sorted force-node and edge sets. pos values are integer world units (1 = 1 px at zoom 1). pin.<pid>=1 is reserved for v2.

plan.eink_and_performance:
MEASURED WAVEFORMS (24-27 C): DU 188 ms, GL16 271 ms, GC16 341 ms (the whole panel). DU is 294 ms when cold. CPU figures are host times x20.

REFRESH PLAN
- Gesture: nothing is drawn while the fingers move; the action's own refresh is the feedback. Recognition costs under 20 us per frame, and firing on lift adds 13-30 ms.
- Bar open and close: a 1.37 Mpx card. Compose plus copy take about 50-90 ms, then GL16. About 0.35 s, no flash.
- Chip press: an immediate DU invert (app_press_feedback).
- Peek: GL16 of the page area only. A cache hit is about 0.35-0.45 s. A miss adds a pumped load and render, typically 0.1-0.3 s and up to 1.2 s.
- Commit: one GC16, which resets the 30-count. Cancel: GL16, or GC16 after 3 or more peeks. Back: GL16.
- Eye: GL16 of the button, plus the union of the area rects, flushed separately when far apart.
- Link long press: the four border strips by DU, with their own app_flush, then the card by GL16, never one union. On close: GL16 of the card and strips.
- Link mode: strip GL16; lasso DU per batch; on lift, GL16 of the lasso's box union.
- Link to..., Find and every keyboard: kbhost.
- Index map: open and close GC16; selection GL16 of small rects; pan and zoom DU at most every 180 ms, then GL16 at release.
- Smart shapes: preview DU, cancel DU, commit through the normal settle. Never GL16 or a toast while the pen is down (pen_leave's wait).
- Gestures record card: GL16 of its reason line only.

FLASH BUDGET
- The every-30th-UI-refresh promotion (app.c:931) stays, because writing's GL16 settles count toward it, and an area-weighted rule would change ghost cleanup under writing.
- GC16 is used only for deliberate screen changes: commit, go to a page, the Pages view, map open and close, theme, invert.
- Each commit's GC16 resets the counter, so heavy bar use costs at most one surprise flash per roughly ten sessions without a commit. Revisit only after device testing.

KEYBOARD LAG STAYS FIXED (kbhost, step 5; adopt the other lane's helper if it lands first)
- Draw only when the field or a key changed, never on an unchanged move (pagesview.c:344-345 redraws on every move today).
- Present the field, then the key, as separate small DU flushes.
- One GL16 settle 900 ms after typing pauses.
- Toast floor at the keyboard's top. It docks top or bottom, as asked.
- Never hosted inside a full-screen compose: the Pages view redraws everything per call (editor.c:672-675).
- The keyboard.draws probe is asserted in every scenario that types.

NEVER BLOCK THE PEN (its evdev buffer overflows after about 100 ms)
- No MXCFB_WAIT_FOR_UPDATE_SUBMISSION, no second wait on a marker, no new display calls. Screens only app_invalidate; app_flush presents. The only wait stays pen_leave before a non-DU refresh.
- Pumped or split:
  - page renders every 64 rows;
  - page reads (new: store_read_page takes a pump callback every 256 strokes, used by peek, prefetch and idle migration);
  - shape dabs every 8 points;
  - map edges every 64;
  - layout every 2 steps, with big layouts in a bgjob child;
  - prefetch one 160-row band per idle tick;
  - idle migration one page per idle tick.
- A sim probe, main.longest_unpumped_ms, is asserted under 100 ms in the big-notebook, prefetch and migration scenarios.
- input_pump drains touch into touchgest, and frames carry kernel SYN times, so a backlog after a render neither bunches a swipe, nor fakes a hold, nor overflows the touch buffer.
- The device scan's busy flag counts every down contact, so its 330-370 ms block never starts mid-gesture.
- light_get never runs on the input path; light_cached replaces it there.

PRIMITIVES (step 6)
- canvas_line_aa becomes row-span: bit-identical, about 40x faster on long edges (0.02 against 0.82 ms per edge on the host). This is a prerequisite for the map.
- canvas_dash_rect(r, thick, on, off, halo), canvas_dash_poly for the lasso, canvas_disc_pattern(cx, cy, r, level) (4x4 Bayer on 2x2 cells) and canvas_slash.
- Everything new is 1-bit-safe.

MEMORY
- Canvas LRU: at most 3 x 4.6 MB.
- Map canvas: 4.6 MB, only while open.
- Shape region copy: at most 4.6 MB, only during a hold.
- Graph arrays: about 2000 x 32 B.
- Every allocation failure has a slower path that draws the same pixels.

LIVE VIEW: it streams App.screen before the toast and chip (app.c:933), so viewers see the bar, the card, the eye and the map, as they see the panel. Excluding them would need live_push skip rects; this is noted, not done.

owner_questions.question: In the Links bar, does each row stand for an Index entry or for one link?

owner_questions.recommended: One row per Index entry, with ×N
owner_questions.why: Your brief says the bar shows 'the index entries that are linked to in that particular page'. A destination listed once reads like an index. Deleting one particular link stays exact through the long press on the page, and Undo covers the group delete.

owner_questions.question: While you hop between links in the bar, which page's links does it list?
options: The page you started on, until you stay (tap the page) or go back (X, two fingers down, Back)
The page you are looking at, so you can walk a chain
owner_questions.why: 'Tap outside the hotbar to confirm' means something only if the bar is a look from where you were. You can compare several targets, and the way home is always one tap. To follow a chain, you stay on a page and swipe up again.

owner_questions.question: When you rename from a link, what gets renamed?
options: The target page's name in the Index, everywhere it appears (the Index, the tiles, the map, the PDF outline). On an unnamed page the button reads 'Add page 20 to the Index...', which makes it an entry and a section start.
A separate label for that link only, stored in links.ini; page names stay as they are
owner_questions.why: Your brief treats links as Index entries, and keeping one name per place keeps the bar, the Index, the map and the PDF in agreement. Navigation everywhere. Two-finger scrolling is lost when sideways or zoomed in.
Navigation only from the edge bands, even upright
owner_questions.recommended: Scroll mid-screen, navigate from the edge bands
owner_questions.why: Upright at the fitted view nothing scrolls, so 'two fingers down opens Pages' works anywhere, exactly as you wrote it. Elsewhere this keeps vertical scrolling. A drag that starts at a scroll limit never opens anything by surprise, and a one-time tip teaches the edge.

Only your two
Also two-finger tap for Undo and three-finger tap for Redo

owner_questions.question: What does 'record a gesture' mean in Settings > Gestures?

Draw any shape you like (free-form matching)

Only Shapes. Links opens by gesture, a hold on the page chip, or a button in the Pages view
Neither: Shapes only in the tool picker

owner_questions.question: Should pen-button gestures be recorded in the same Gestures sheet, instead of the pen plan's separate Pen button sheet?
options: One action-first Gestures sheet for touch and pen; gestures.ini absorbs the planned pen.ini. The held-button cycler stays a Settings row.
Keep a separate, gesture-first Pen button sheet
owner_questions.why: You asked for one place where anything the controller can do is assigned. It is one file and one rule: per action, at most one touch gesture and one pen gesture. Both files are unreleased, so nothing breaks.

risks: Pen near. 'Write, lift, swipe' often starts with the pen still hovering. The first build rejects multi-finger gestures while the pen hovers, so the headline gesture can feel refused. The rate-limited 'Move the pen away' toast keeps it from feeling like a hang, and step 19 relaxes the rule from the device log. The owner must test this in build P2.
The panel's slot count, TOUCH_MAJOR range and palm flagging are unknown. Three-finger gestures and the palm-size guard stay hidden or log-only until the step-1 log is read.
Sideways or zoomed in, navigation needs the edge band, which is harder to teach than 'anywhere'. Mitigations: the one-time tip, the Gestures sheet footer, and the visible Links button and page chip.

How a two-finger drag feels will change: the zoom no longer drifts while panning, swipes no longer move the view, and timing switches to kernel time. k_pinch_gate guards the dead zone but not the feel; the owner tests it.

Peek state could leak into edits. Mitigated by design: a peek is a display state, S->index, S->page, history and hit tests stay on the origin, and every way out commits or cancels explicitly. Scenarios cover autosave, sleep and leaving the editor during a peek.

Peek cost and memory: a cold peek of a dense or PDF page can still take up to 1.2 s; GL16 peeks build up ghosting until the commit's or cancel's GC16; the cache takes up to about 14 MB. Prefetch must stop at the first contact. Kindle RAM headroom is not measured, and every allocation has a slower fallback that draws the same pixels.

Migration is a one-way rewrite of the owner's links.ini. Using the 7 mm grown box, or counting erase strokes, would silently change tappable areas, so fixtures are copies of real device notebooks. If f9d13f5 is ever used again it carries area lines only up to 16 KiB (about 430 links), then goes read-only there and never overwrites the file.

Areas are invisible to every other reader (older versions, the share page, Live view's page layer). Only the PDF carries them, as invisible /Link annotations, so a user may think links were lost. The eye only helps on the device.
Smallest-wins replaces last-drawn-wins, so beta.5 links with overlapping boxes may resolve differently. This is acceptable while beta.5 is unreleased, and test_nav covers it.

ACT_LINK writes a notebook-wide sidecar from inside a page's history. A failed save must drop the step after nav_load restores the file, never leave history pointing at a change that did not happen. Redo after the target page is deleted must do nothing.
Renaming from a link can create a section start, which moves the Index tab's section highlight for later pages. The button wording and the toast name it, but it may still surprise.

Smart shapes: very large or slow handwriting can show a preview and then revert (two DU frames). The corpus is small (47 strokes, read-time stamps). The region-render preview may be slow on dense pages; the tile backup is the planned fallback if the shape-log shows renders over about 300 ms.

The Index map: large layouts run in bgjob's single queue, so a PDF mirror can delay them, and the seed placement must look acceptable meanwhile. Floats differ between arm64 and armv7, so tests use invariants only. The canvas_line_aa rewrite touches every Gothic drawing and must stay bit-identical.
Panel growth to 13 buttons, and the moved Settings bottom row, break raw coordinate taps. Step 4's symbolic taps, and the updated 10 taps plus y_all_screens.qs:631, must land before or with them.
The Buttons sheet becomes parametrized by BindKind, which can regress the Controller flow. v_controller*.qs must stay green at every step.
The pen plan's references are stale and its lane is unimplemented. Folding pen.ini into gestures.ini, and its actions into the registry, requires that lane to adopt this design (P7).
A new keyboard surface that bypasses kbhost brings back the Index keyboard lag. keyboard.draws is asserted in every typing scenario.
Live view streams App.screen, so viewers see the bar, the card, the eye and the map. That may surprise someone streaming their notes.
